approachQuestion.prompt:
Opposite Displays. Return whether binary tree B is the exact left-right reflection of binary tree A, including labels and missing-child positions. Either tree may be empty; repeated integer labels are allowed.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: A=4(2(-,7(-,-)),9(-,-)), B=4(9(-,-),2(7(-,-),-)). Output: true. Example 2: Input: A=1(2(-,-),-), B=1(2(-,-),-). Output: false: a reflection must move the child to the other side. Example 3: Input: A=-, B=-. Output: true.

Constraints: the combined node count n is at most 200000; labels are signed 32-bit integers. Both trees are immutable with child pointers only, no cycles or shared nodes. No ordering or balance is promised. Depth-first and level-order comparisons with different shape-dependent storage are both acceptable.

options.text: Start a depth-first stack with the roots as a pair. Accept two missing pointers, reject exactly one missing pointer or unequal labels, and otherwise schedule (A.left,B.right) and (A.right,B.left).
options.feedback: The scheduled pairs are precisely the positions that must correspond in a reflection, and null checks enforce shape.

options.text: Use a queue of root and cross-child pairs, with the same null and label checks.
options.feedback: The order changes but the obligations do not. Width-dependent queue storage is an acceptable alternative.

options.text: Recursively build a complete token array for every subtree, with labels and null markers; reverse child order for B. At every parent concatenate copied child arrays, then compare the root arrays.
options.feedback: Null markers make this exact for every tree. Recopying full encodings at ancestors repeats work on a chain; direct pair comparison avoids those copies.

options.text: Compare roots, then compare A.left with B.left and A.right with B.right, including nulls.
options.feedback: This tests ordinary equality. It accepts Example 2, which is not a reflection.

feedback.reason: Compare reflected positions as node pairs, including missing-child positions.
details: Push the roots as one pair. Pop pairs in depth-first order. Continue for two nulls, return false for one null or unequal labels, and otherwise push the two cross-child pairs. Return true when no obligations remain. Store pointer pairs rather than copied encodings.

Mirror comparison pairs left with right and right with left. Equal labels alone are insufficient when one paired child is null. Two nulls satisfy that structural obligation without scheduling more work.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed depth-first pair stack, even after choosing the queue. Let n >= 1 be the combined node count and h the greater tree height in nodes. What is the tight worst-case pair? Include pending pairs, including null pairs, and scalar state; exclude both input trees and the Boolean result.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

feedback.reason: Compare each paired node once with a height-bounded stack of obligations.
details: Each node belongs to at most one comparison; null obligations are also linear in number. Pending cross-child pairs use O(h) stack entries, and matching branching trees can attain that scale.
Two roots reflect exactly when they are both missing, or have equal labels and both cross-child pairs reflect. The algorithm checks these necessary and sufficient obligations.

“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Each node belongs to at most one comparison; null obligations are also linear in number. Pending cross-child pairs use O(h) stack entries, and matching branching trees can attain that scale.
“O(n²) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Completed subtrees are not scanned again; nesting the control flow does not itself multiply the node visits.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The live explicit stack is auxiliary memory and can grow with tree height.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This is a looser upper bound since h <= n; the height-sensitive bound is tighter and no full node table is retained.
